answers.question: How does Redis caching work?
answers.answer_text: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used as a cache. It supports TTL (time-to-live) to expire stale keys automatically. When memory fills up, eviction policies like LRU remove oldest entries. This dramatically reduces latency compared to hitting the database.
